objective: Audit which archived rerun-based DAFoam conclusions could have been silently warm-started, now that the wrapper is proven to write the primal end state back into time 0 on every run
rationale: Found executing the entry-8 A3 arm (prereg addendum f77b2607, result 0b4f3005): pyDAFoam writes the converged primal end state back into the time-0 directory at run end (the time-0 velocity field bit-identical to the time-1000 velocity field after the run), so every SUBSEQUENT run of the same case directory silently warm-starts from the previous run's converged fields while its controlDict still says startFrom startTime 0 -- the cold start you assumed is not the start that ran. Separately, renameSolution (the pyDAFoam wrapper, line 1543) hard-raises on a leftover 0.0001 time directory, killing reruns before the adjoint. Measured consequences on the A3 sweep case: a warm primal ran 1000 steps in 10.13 s where the cold run of the identical configuration takes the record wall, and the warm end state differed from the record writeout by up to 2.2 percent of the velocity maximum -- two different near-converged plateaus of the same flow, which is exactly the state dimension of the L-40 hazard class: an instrument silently not measuring what its configuration says it measures. Any archived conclusion that compared two runs of one case directory in sequence (mitigation sweeps, reordering 2x2s, option A/B arms) could have had a warm second arm linearizing about a different state than its cold first arm
gate: A log-forensics audit, no solver compute. Inventory: every archived case directory under certonomous-runs and the repo work dirs that carries two or more solver runs of the same case (mitigation sequences, A/B arms, sweep variants), enumerated from the run logs and time-directory timestamps already on disk. Cold-vs-warm discrimination per run, from signatures this campaign validated: (a) primal wall per 1000 steps -- warm runs are an order of magnitude faster (10.13 s vs record-scale cold walls on the same mesh); (b) the first Time step continuity errors line -- cold from uniform starts at the 1e-1 scale (0.597 measured), warm starts orders lower; (c) presence of a 0.0001 rename or a renameSolution failure in the log; (d) mtimes of processor time-0 fields versus the run's own window. Output: a per-conclusion verdict table -- COLD-CLEAN, WARM-CONTAMINATED (with which arm was warm), or INDETERMINATE (logs insufficient) -- plus, for each WARM-CONTAMINATED conclusion, whether the conclusion compared KSP behavior (robust to plateau choice unless near-marginal) or state-sensitive quantities (gradient values, residual plateaus, objective values -- where the 2.2 percent state drift can matter). The B3/CBFS reordering 2x2, the D3 sweep variant arms, and the R5 matrix dumps are the named first targets since each reran one case directory repeatedly
cost_basis: measured-analog: log forensics only, zero solver core-minutes; the discriminating signatures are already validated on the A3 sweep case (attempt-1 warm vs attempt-2/TPC1 cold logs, all preserved); agent time approximately one session for the inventory plus verdict table
expected_knowledge_gain: Either the archived rerun-based record is certified cold-clean case by case, or specific conclusions are flagged as warm-contaminated with the direction of contamination named -- and the wrapper hazard itself enters the family guidelines either way: cold-start restoration (move 0.0001 and the overwritten time-0 aside, decomposePar -fields from pristine serial 0) becomes a standing pre-run step for any archived-case rerun
citations: The A3 sub-LU sweep pre-registration, addendum 1 (commit f77b2607): the falsified inert-leftovers claim, the bit-identical 0-vs-1000 proof, and the 2.2 percent warm-state drift measurement
The A3 sub-LU result record (0b4f3005, 11b90d25): the warm 10.13 s primal vs the cold primal, and the cold-start continuity-error signature 0.597
The pyDAFoam wrapper renameSolution at line 1543, the hard-raise on leftover 0.0001
The L-40 hazard class precedent: an instrument silently not doing what its configuration says
launch_prompt: pydafoam silent warm-start audit. Read A3_SUBLU_SWEEP_PREREGISTRATION.md addendum 1 and the gate of this proposal first. Log forensics only, zero solver compute. Inventory every archived case dir with multiple runs, apply the four cold-vs-warm signatures, produce the per-conclusion verdict table (COLD-CLEAN / WARM-CONTAMINATED / INDETERMINATE), starting with the B3 reordering 2x2, the D3 sweep variants, and the R5 dumps. Add the cold-start restoration step to FAMILY_SUPERVISION_GUIDELINES.md on completion. No conclusion is rewritten by this audit; flags go to the chief for regrade decisions.
decision_note: approved by chief ruling 3 of the entry-8 epilogue (14d57c8e), as priced: log-forensics only, zero solver core-min; executed by the filing agent per the same ruling
outcome: Executed as priced (zero solver core-min, log forensics; WARMSTART_AUDIT.md 9bb948b2). Nine-row verdict table: every record-grade conclusion COLD-CLEAN -- the W4 reordering/unblock studies ran each arm in its own staged case copy with bit-identical first continuity errors (state-controlled by construction), and the entry-8 chain carries in-log cold proofs. Two WARM flags, neither overturning anything: the D3 n15 variant-lever nulls (logs lost with the interrupted session, mechanism certain, nothing currently cites them, cold rerun required before any future citation) and the R5/M6 matrix dumps (state ~2 percent warm-drifted, order-of-magnitude conclusions robust, flagged for chief discretion). Priced signature (a) fast-warm-primal found INVALID and disclosed -- cold and warm primals both take ~10 s at this rung; the validated discriminator is the first continuity-error value (55x cold/warm separation, bit-stable across six cold runs). Guidelines section 8 added (ccf18d2f): cold-start restoration recipe, in-log cold proof requirement, staged-copy pattern. Regrade decisions left to the chief per the proposal's terms.
